# S508 — The plan flags a backticked Check entry that is not a runnable command

When the run plan reads a slice's Check commands, it warns about each backticked entry whose first word is not a command it can find on PATH or a path to an executable in the worktree, naming the line, so the spec is fixed before the run starts.

**Findings:** 2026-11-18 to 11-20: three runs stopped at slice checks because a Check section had backticked text that is not a command: S392 (a test name in prose ran the race test), S384 ("Contract: relay v13": exec "Contract:" not found), S318 ("internal/cli": fork/exec permission denied). Each cost a stop and a hand fix in the worktree. · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**2026-11-20** — Plans warn about non-command Check entries without refusing start; env-prefixed commands get no false warning and a bare name that exists only in the worktree is warned, as os/exec cannot run it.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

ork runs every backticked entry in a Check section (`internal/engine/brief.go:640-710`, `sliceCheckCommands`). Prose with backticked paths or quoted output reaches the slice checks and stops the run late. The plan already prints warnings and the spec check reads the slice first, so the cheapest place to catch it is the plan.
